entries.description:
An object of another program, reached by its name in the Windows registry (a ProgID such as "ADODB.Connection" or a fiscal register driver's). Its properties and methods are looked up when they are used, so nothing about the object has to be known when the module is compiled.

WINDOWS ONLY. The type exists on every platform, so a module that creates one compiles on macOS and Linux too; there `New COMObject` is refused when it runs, with "COM objects are available on Windows only". On Windows it works in the thin client and on the application server.

VALUES CROSS BOTH WAYS by kind: a number goes as an integer when it is one (as a double otherwise) and comes back exactly, CY and DECIMAL included; a string, a boolean, a date, Null and Undefined go as themselves; an Array goes as an array and an array comes back as an Array (nested, for more dimensions); another COM object goes as itself. A value with no COM spelling - a reference, a structure - is refused with its type named.

AN ARGUMENT the member declares as an output is written back into the caller's variable. An argument left out (`Obj.Method(a, , c)`) is sent as missing, so the object uses its own default.

FOR EACH walks a collection the object exposes (ADO `Fields`, MSXML node lists, the keys of `Scripting.Dictionary`).

A FAILED CALL is raised with the object and the member named, and the object's own description of what went wrong.
entries.parameters: progId - the name the class is registered under. One that is not registered is refused, and the message names it.

entries.description:
Calls `handler` each time the object raises the event `eventName`. The events are those of the object's default event interface; an object that has none, or no event by that name, is refused.

The handler receives the event's arguments in order; an argument the object passes by reference takes the value the handler left in it.

An event is handled on the thread that owns the object: while the script is inside a call to the object, or, in the thin client, whenever it is idle. A handler that raises an error raises it from the call during which the event came.
entries.parameters:
eventName - the event's name, as the object declares it.
handler - a function: `Function(arg1, arg2) { ... }`.

entries.description: Stops calling the handler given for `eventName`. When no handler is left the platform disconnects from the object's events.
